design_status: Sequential exploratory replication extension created after reviewing initial campaign progress; all five new seeds, matched architecture/split cells, evaluation policy and continuation rule were fixed before launching any of these 20 runs.
question: Do the base-versus-tiny and identity-split comparisons persist across five additional independent initialization seeds per model/split cell?
objective: supervised contrastive loss with a 64-dimensional feature head
architecture_ablation: tiny uses the same objective, feature dimension, split, batch composition, augmentation, and seeds as base; only channel widths change
split_method: identity-disjoint 80/20 split stratified by image-count decile
cap_extension_rule: After initial training, resume any run that reaches epoch 30 with fewer than five epochs since its last validation-AUC improvement to a total target of epoch 40. If a resumed run reaches epoch 40 with fewer than five no-improvement epochs, continue the same run to epoch 50. These are continuations, not additional independent seeds; retain full histories and report extensions explicitly.
selection_and_test_policy: All seeds and comparisons are specified before inspecting this extension's results. Checkpoint selection and decision thresholds use each run's identity-disjoint validation pairs only. Export and score float and full-integer INT8 TFLite models on that validation set. Do not load the supplied final SurvFace pair annotations or Olivetti. Do not deploy a candidate based on this validation comparison without a separately documented decision and board check.
interpretation_caveats: Best-epoch metrics are validation-selected and are not unbiased test estimates.

Ten matched base/tiny seeds per model/split cell are the target after combining the five earlier matched seeds with this extension; the distinct-seed base split-B cell also contains earlier seeds 20261027-20261031.
Seed variability on fixed identity splits does not create independent test sets.
Pair-bootstrap intervals resample pairs and may be optimistic because pairs share identities and images; identity-cluster intervals are also reported.
Recorded runtime is wall-clock and can include data loading and host idle/sleep gaps, so it is not active CPU time or a throughput measurement.
The five-seed pilot used different TensorFlow thread settings and remains separate.

evaluation.format: float TFLite and full signed-integer INT8 TFLite
